item.title: Go Internationalization in 2026: go-i18n vs gotext vs golang.org/x/text
item.description: Adding a second language to a Go service looks like a two-hour task until you hit plural rules. English has two forms, Polish has four, Arabic has six, and Japanese has one — and the moment a product manager asks for “3 pliki” versus “5 plików” you discover that fmt.Sprintf with an if count == 1 branch is not an internationalization strategy. Go has no blessed answer in the standard library; there are three credible packages and they disagree about almost everything: message format, translation workflow, and who owns plural logic.
